terms.gloss: I must go, I must be off
terms.grammar: gerundive of necessity, impersonal, with the person in the dative; so nōbīs eundum est, we must go
evidence: Plaut. Am. 1.3.29: clam illūc redeundum est mihi (Lewis & Short s.v. illic)
Traupman 16: quīn nunc abeundum mihi est
terms.comment: Literally “there must be going away by me”: the verb is impersonal and the person goes into the dative.

terms.gloss: it’s time for me to go
evidence: Cic. Tusc. 1.99: tempus est jam hinc abīre mē (Lewis & Short s.v. tempus)
Plaut. Capt. prol. 67: abeō: valēte (Lewis & Short s.v. valeō)
terms.comment: The plain present announces the leaving, often with valē.

phrases.latin: Quīn nunc abeundum mihi est. Valē.
phrases.english: Well, I must go now. Goodbye.

phrases.latin: tempus est jam hinc abīre mē
phrases.english: it is time now for me to go hence

sources: Lewis & Short: abeo · Lewis & Short: tempus
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 16–17, each phrase checked against the searchable text of the book.
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
